traceability.evidence: Story file exists and matches the assessed spec: docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md, including requirements REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-FORMAT, REQ-DEEP-SECTION, REQ-DEEP-CACHE, REQ-DEEP-ERROR and the listed Acceptance Criteria.,Rule implementation: src/rules/valid-req-reference.ts defines the ESLint rule `valid-req-reference` with meta.docs.description "Validate that @req annotations reference existing requirements in referenced story files" and recommended severity 'error'. The rule delegates to helpers via `Program: createValidReqReferenceProgramVisitor(context)`. Message templates: - reqMissing: "Requirement '{{reqId}}' not found in '{{storyPath}}'" - invalidPath: "Invalid story path '{{storyPath}}'" Both messages are annotated in JSDoc with @story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md and docs/stories/007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING.story.md and map to REQ-ERROR-* requirements, satisfying REQ-DEEP-ERROR and the User Experience acceptance criterion for clear, contextual error messages.,Deep-validation logic and caching: src/rules/helpers/valid-req-reference-helpers.ts encapsulates the core behavior and is annotated with: - `@supports docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md REQ-DEEP-PARSE REQ-DEEP-MATCH REQ-DEEP-CACHE` Key functions: - extractStoryPath: parses JSDoc-style comment text to find `@story ` lines (REQ-DEEP-PARSE over annotations). - validateAndResolveStoryPath: rejects story paths containing ".." or absolute paths using path.isAbsolute, and enforces that resolved paths stay under `cwd` before returning the resolved path; otherwise reports `invalidPath` (integrates path safety from 006.0 and contributes to REQ-DEEP-CACHE / path validation). - loadAndCacheRequirements: `fs.readFileSync` of the story file, scans content with `/REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g` and stores all matches into a `Set` in a `Map<string, Set>` cache keyed by resolved path; on any error it catches and caches an empty Set. This implements parsing across the entire markdown file (independent of section or list style) and per-Program caching (REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-FORMAT, REQ-DEEP-SECTION, REQ-DEEP-CACHE, Error Handling AC by not crashing on I/O errors). - checkRequirementExists: checks `reqSet.has(reqId)` and, if false, reports `reqMissing` with `{ reqId, storyPath }` (REQ-DEEP-MATCH and REQ-DEEP-ERROR). - extractReqIdFromLine: parses `@req` lines into IDs (REQ-DEEP-PARSE of annotation format). - resolveStoryAndRequirements: composes validateAndResolveStoryPath + loadAndCacheRequirements and returns {resolvedStoryPath, reqSet}, centralising path validation + caching (integration with file validation). - validateReqLine: wires a single `@req` line to path resolution, cache usage, and existence check. If storyPath is null or invalid, it no-ops; if resolution succeeds, it calls checkRequirementExists (Core Functionality AC). - parseImplementsLine and validateImplementsLine: support `@supports ` lines, parsing storyPath and multiple requirement IDs, then resolving and validating all IDs against the cached Set (integrates deep validation with multi-story support from 010.2 and supports multiple requirement IDs per line; contributes to REQ-DEEP-FORMAT and Integration AC). - handleAnnotationLine / processCommentLines / handleComment / processAllComments: iterate all comment lines from `sourceCode.getAllComments()`, track the current `@story` path across comments, and dispatch `@req` and `@supports` lines for validation while reusing the shared `reqCache` (REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-CACHE and integration with existing annotation parsing). - programListener and createValidReqReferenceProgramVisitor: set up a per-Program `reqCache` and derive `cwd = process.cwd()`, then, on Program enter, call processAllComments. This ensures each ESLint run parses each referenced story file at most once, satisfying REQ-DEEP-CACHE and Integration AC (works within ESLint’s Program lifecycle).,Requirement formats and story-file structures (Quality Standards, REQ-DEEP-FORMAT, REQ-DEEP-SECTION): - loadAndCacheRequirements uses a simple regex `/REQ-[A-Z0-9-]+/g` over the entire markdown content and does not depend on headings, sections, bullets, or numbering. This means requirement IDs are detected whether they appear as plain lines, in bullet lists, or in numbered lists, and in any section (Requirements, Acceptance Criteria, etc.). - Fixtures confirm support for at least bullet-list formats and multiple sections: - tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md contains a "## Requirements" section with bullet items `- REQ-BULLET-LIST - a requirement in bullet list format` and `- REQ-ANOTHER - another requirement`. The valid and invalid tests for this file show deep validation correctly recognizing and matching these IDs. - tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md and tests/fixtures/story_multi_b.md contain bullet lists with IDs `REQ-SHARED-ID`, `REQ-ONLY-A`, `REQ-ONLY-B`. The rule correctly validates multiple IDs per story and treats the same ID in multiple files as independently valid, demonstrating tolerance of different story structures and multi-story setups. Because the parser ignores markdown structure and just finds `REQ-*` tokens, IDs in Acceptance Criteria or numbered lists would be handled the same way, satisfying the "various formats and story file structures" Acceptance Criterion in practice.,Dedicated tests for this story: tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts - File header: - `@story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md` - `@req REQ-DEEP-PARSE - Verify valid-req-reference rule enforces existing requirement content` - plus @story/@req references to 007.0-DEV-ERROR-REPORTING for error behavior. - `describe('Valid Req Reference Rule (Story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION)', ...)` ties the suite directly to this story. - Valid cases (Core Functionality, REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-FORMAT, Integration AC): - `[REQ-DEEP-PARSE] valid requirement reference existing in story file`: uses `// @story docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md` and `// @req REQ-PLUGIN-STRUCTURE`, confirming that when a referenced requirement exists in that story file, no error is reported. - `[REQ-DEEP-BULLET] valid bullet list requirement existing in bullet story fixture`: references `// @story tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md` and `// @req REQ-BULLET-LIST`, demonstrating that bullet-list-defined requirements are correctly recognized. - Two `[REQ-DEEP-IMPLEMENTS]` tests exercise `@supports` with multiple IDs and multiple story files (story_multi_a.md and story_multi_b.md), confirming that deep validation honors multiple requirement IDs per line and scopes them per story file. - Invalid cases (REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-ERROR, Error Handling AC, Integration): - `[REQ-DEEP-MATCH] missing requirement in story file`: expects `messageId: 'reqMissing'` with `data: { reqId: 'REQ-NON-EXISTENT', storyPath: 'docs/stories/001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP.story.md' }`. This verifies that missing requirement IDs produce a clear, contextual error message (Core Functionality + User Experience AC + REQ-DEEP-ERROR). - Path validation tests for both @story and @supports: - Path traversal via `../docs/stories/...` triggers `invalidPath` with the offending storyPath. - Absolute path via `/absolute/path/docs/stories/...` likewise triggers `invalidPath`. - Similar tests for `@supports ../tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md REQ-SHARED-ID` expect `invalidPath`. These confirm integration with the 006.0 path safety model and clear error reporting for invalid paths. - Bullet fixture negative: missing `REQ-MISSING-BULLET` in story_bullet.md triggers `reqMissing` with appropriate data, proving correct handling of bullet-based requirements when they are absent.,Fixtures used by deep validation: - tests/fixtures/story_bullet.md: - Contains a "## Requirements" section with bullet items such as `- REQ-BULLET-LIST - a requirement in bullet list format`. - Demonstrates that the parser detects requirements in bullet lists, satisfying a key part of REQ-DEEP-FORMAT and Quality Standards. - tests/fixtures/story_multi_a.md and tests/fixtures/story_multi_b.md: - Both contain bullet lists of requirement IDs; each includes `REQ-SHARED-ID` plus a unique ID (`REQ-ONLY-A` or `REQ-ONLY-B`). - The rule and tests confirm that the same ID may exist in multiple story files and is validated independently per story path (IDs scoped to story files), aligning with the documented behavior and multi-story deep validation expectations.,Documentation for this rule (Documentation AC): docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md - Annotated with: - `@story docs/stories/010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION.story.md` - `@req REQ-DEEP-PARSE`, `@req REQ-DEEP-MATCH`, `@req REQ-DEEP-PATH` - Describes behavior in detail, addressing Acceptance Criteria: - Explains that the rule "Enforces that `@req` and `@supports` annotations reference existing requirements in story files" (Core Functionality) and protects against invalid paths. - States that it parses referenced story files to extract requirement IDs like `REQ-XXX-YYY`, and validates that each `@req` and each `@supports` requirement ID exists in the corresponding story file (REQ-DEEP-PARSE, REQ-DEEP-MATCH, REQ-DEEP-FORMAT, REQ-DEEP-SECTION, Integration AC). - Documents the two error types with explanations: `invalidPath` for paths with `..` or absolute paths, and `reqMissing` when a requirement is not found (User Experience + REQ-DEEP-ERROR + Error Handling AC descriptions). - Provides correct and incorrect code examples showing allowed and disallowed usage of `@story`/`@req` and `@supports`, including examples of path traversal and absolute paths. - Explains how `@story` & `@req` interact with `@supports` in multi-story scenarios, and that requirement IDs only need to be unique within a single story file. This gives concrete examples of supported deep-validation formats and integration with 010.2 multi-story behavior, satisfying the "Documentation" acceptance criterion at a practical level.,Integration with existing annotation and file validation logic (Integration AC): - The rule operates solely on comments via context.getSourceCode().getAllComments(), interpreting `@story`, `@req`, and `@supports` tags, which integrates cleanly with the annotation formats validated by the 005.0-DEV-ANNOTATION-VALIDATION story (the `valid-annotation-format` rule). The deep validator relies on annotations being correctly formatted identifiers and paths, without duplicating that formatting logic. - Path validation in validateAndResolveStoryPath mirrors the safety constraints from the 006.0-DEV-FILE-VALIDATION story (rejecting path traversal and absolute paths, and ensuring resolved paths stay within `cwd`). Actual existence checks are provided by the dedicated `valid-story-reference` rule (Story 006.0), which is tested separately; together, these rules compose to provide both existence checks and deep content validation. - The `@supports` parsing and validation logic references Story 010.2-DEV-MULTI-STORY-SUPPORT explicitly and uses the same `@supports ` structure, confirming that deep validation works as an additional layer on top of the multi-story and annotation-format infrastructure instead of replacing it.,Error Handling behavior (Error Handling AC, REQ-DEEP-ERROR): - loadAndCacheRequirements wraps file I/O in a try/catch. On any error (missing file, permission issue, malformed content, etc.), it stores an empty `Set` in the cache instead of throwing. This ensures the ESLint process does not crash on malformed or unreadable story files and that subsequent validations behave consistently (they will simply not find any REQ IDs and may report reqMissing as appropriate). - validateReqLine and validateImplementsLine short-circuit gracefully if storyPath is null/invalid or if resolveStoryAndRequirements returns null `reqSet`, so malformed annotations or invalid paths do not cause runtime errors in the rule. - Combined with the clear `reqMissing` and `invalidPath` messages and dedicated tests for path traversal and absolute paths, this satisfies the "Gracefully handles malformed story files, missing sections, or parsing errors" Acceptance Criterion in terms of robustness and user feedback.,Test execution (current run, confirming behavior still holds): - Command: `npm test -- --runInBand --verbose --testPathPatterns tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts` - Output excerpt: - `PASS tests/rules/valid-req-reference.test.ts` - Suite: `Valid Req Reference Rule (Story 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION)` - 10 tests passed (4 valid cases, 6 invalid cases) covering correct requirement presence, bullet-list handling, multi-story/multi-requirement `@supports` usage, missing requirements, and invalid paths. - This confirms that the implementation for Story 010.0 is currently passing all its dedicated tests and remains in a working state.
traceability.notes: All requirements and acceptance criteria for 010.0-DEV-DEEP-VALIDATION are satisfied by the current implementation. The `valid-req-reference` rule and its helpers implement deep validation of requirement IDs by reading story files, extracting REQ identifiers, and validating `@req` and `@supports` annotations against that content, with per-Program caching. The implementation is annotation-format-agnostic, so it naturally supports different story structures and requirement presentations (plain lines, bullet lists, etc.), and fixtures verify at least bullet-list formats and multi-story scenarios. Error handling is robust (I/O errors do not crash ESLint, and clear `reqMissing`/`invalidPath` diagnostics are emitted instead). Documentation in docs/rules/valid-req-reference.md explains the behavior, error modes, and provides examples of supported usage. Targeted tests for this story all pass under Jest, and the broader test suite also passes, so this story is fully implemented and verified.
